name: 4-AcO-MiPT
toxicities: The toxicity and long-term health effects of 4-AcO-MiPT have not been studied in any scientific context and the exact toxic dose is unknown, because 4-AcO-MiPT is a research chemical with a very short history of human use. Anecdotal evidence suggests that trying it only at low to moderate doses and rarely has no negative health effects, though this cannot be fully guaranteed.
effectsSummary: 4-AcO-MiPT's body high as a pleasant, warm, soft and encompassing tingling that builds after onset and peaks at the peak of the experience. Effects come from a subjective-effects index built on anecdotal user reports, and adverse effects become more likely at higher doses, potentially including addiction, serious injury or death.

metabolism: 4-AcO-MiPT as the acetylated form of 4-HO-MiPT, and says these substances are generally assumed to act mainly as prodrugs of their respective hydroxylated counterparts, while noting that whether they have their own intrinsic activity is disputed. summary: 4-AcO-MiPT is a quite potent synthetic psychedelic tryptamine, the acetylated form of 4-HO-MiPT, and is generally assumed to act as a prodrug of its hydroxylated counterpart. It has been related to having shroom-like visuals, yet without much bodyload; it is very hydroscopic and seems to be quite safe in dosing. Its effects are similar to those of 2C-B. The archived page gives no specific human metabolic finding or pathway.
